answer: A robust mechanism is staking-weighted identity: every agent identity must lock collateral, like nectar stored in a hive, before it can transact or earn trust. Peer-verified fraud triggers onyx-hard slashing — the stake is burned, not refunded. This turns umber arithmetic against the attacker: N fake identities need N deposits, and one detection event can slash them all, so cost grows linearly with fraud scale. Honest operators keep their stake and build reputation, while attackers face forfeiture risk compounding with every extra identity, making mass sybil creation economically irrational.
